publications: Effect of Surface Microstructure on Electrochemical Performance of Garnet Solid Electrolytes - Cubic garnet phases based on Al-substituted Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) have high ionic conductivities and exhibit good stability versus metallic lithium, making them of particular interest for use in next-generation rechargeable battery systems. However, high interfacial impedances have precluded their successful utilization in such devices until the present. Careful engineering of the surface microstructure, especially the grain boundaries, is critical to achieving low interfacial resistances and enabling long-term stable cycling with lithium metal. This study presents the fabrication of LLZO heterostructured solid electrolytes, which allowed direct correlation of surface microstructure with the electrochemical characteristics of the interface. Grain orientations and grain boundary distributions of samples with differing microstructures were mapped using high-resolution synchrotron polychromatic X-ray Laue microdiffraction. The electrochemical characteristics are strongly dependent upon surface microstructure, with small grained samples exhibiting much lower interfacial resistances and better cycling behavior than those with larger grain sizes. Low area specific resistances of 37 Ω cm2 were achieved; low enough to ensure stable cycling with minimal polarization losses, thus removing a significant obstacle toward practical implementation of solid electrolytes in high energy density batteries. Show less

The origin of high electrolyte–electrode interfacial resistances in lithium cells containing garnet type solid electrolytes - Dense LLZO (Al-substituted Li7La3Zr2O12) pellets were processed in controlled atmospheres to investigate the relationships between the surface chemistry and interfacial behavior in lithium cells. Laser induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) studies revealed that Li2CO3 was formed on the surface when LLZO pellets were exposed to air. The distribution and thickness of the Li2CO3 layer were estimated by a combination of bulk and surface sensitive techniques with various probing depths. First-principles thermodynamic calculations confirmed that LLZO has an energetic preference to form Li2CO3 in air. Exposure to air and the subsequent formation of Li2CO3 at the LLZO surface is the source of the high interfacial impedances observed in cells with lithium electrodes. Surface polishing can effectively remove Li2CO3 and dramatically improve the interfacial properties. Polished samples in lithium cells had an area specific resistance (ASR) of only 109 Ω cm2 for the LLZO/Li interface, the lowest reported value for Al-substituted LLZO. Galvanostatic cycling results obtained from lithium symmetrical cells also suggest that the quality of the LLZO/lithium interface has a significant impact on the device lifetime. Show less

Distinct Solid-Electrolyte-Interphases on Sn (100) and (001) Electrodes Studied by Soft X-Ray Spectroscopy - Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy with different probe depth was employed to characterize the solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) formed on β-Sn single crystals with two different surface orientations. Based on comparative studies of C-K, O-K, and F-K absorption spectra between the SEIs and reference samples, SEI on Sn (100) mainly consists of porous Li2CO3 species with electrolyte uptake, while SEI on Sn (001) essentially consists of LiF and organic molecules, with a small amount of –CO3 and electrolyte buried inside. Theoretical calculation suggests that Sn (001) surface is more reactive than (100), especially after air exposure. The reactive (001) surface facilitates the decomposition of LiPF6 to form a LiF layer. In contrast, SEI on (100) surface is predominately from the typical decomposition of carbonate-based electrolyte. While the LiF passivates Sn (001) electrode after one cycle, the porous carbonate layer on (100) surface does not prevent further decomposition of electrolyte after many cycles. This leads to drastically different electrochemical behavior and morphology of the two SEIs. Show less

I went through UCLA's Plumbing Systems Design course, completing the course in 1980, and have been doing piping design ever since. Projects have included commercial buildings, hospitals and medical facilities, state park facilities, military installations for all branches of the United States Armed Forces, waterfront facilities such as marinas, wharves, and piers, as well as pump stations and petroleum loading and offloading platforms. I miss drafting on vellum (but not on mylar, thank goodness), but the world has moved on and I've learned instead to use AutoCAD with a dash of MicroStation and a bit of 3D. I'm a published author of fiction, and I enjoy photography as well.

headline: Post-Bar JD Graduate
summary: I have lived in Los Angeles County for the majority of my life, and I am closely aware of the difficulties faced by low-income families and communities. Such experiences have shown me that the efficiency of a justice system can only be gauged when its access is universal; otherwise, persecution and injustices become the norm for those unable to gain access to a supposedly just system. My own family has experienced what such a lack of access to the legal system can result in, facing political prosecution from the Mexican government after the 1988 elections for simply being members of the FDN. Such events should not be allowed to occur within our own justice system, for its allowance jeopardizes our fundamental civil rights. Especially in today's political system when so many political minorities require a strong and fair legal system to ensure they do not become the targets of scapegoating or persecution. It is why I continue committed to aiding marginalized communities using my developed research and writing skills along with increasing legal knowledge. I developed my research and writing skills throughout my undergraduate years as a member of Davis' MUN debate team and the creation of my research paper, A System Unable to Pay for Justice, that I was allowed to present for UC Center Sacramento. My work at Polycoat made professional use of such skills, being tasked to write patent and trademark memos for my employer to determine the best argumentation available. I continue to develop these skills in a professional setting at Caruso School of Law through its year-long Legal Research and Writing course which has given me a greater understanding of legal documents and how to better brief them into workable memos. Through my work with multiple political campaigns and as an intern for the California Democratic Party my interpersonal skills have given me a closer tie to the communities I affect. Through these different experiences, I was responsible for communicating with a wider community whose needs and wants had to be balanced with the goals of our organization to further a relationship of understanding gain trust from the community, and better help work with one another. I believe that my work with local communities has prepared me to meet the work of helping those most disadvantaged and further the goals of any organization to secure and promote access to the justice system. I am confident in my ability to maintain a utilitarian approach to the larger goals of my job and stay attentive to the personal need and empathy required to work with clients.

Galanin, through GalR1 but not GalR2 receptors, decreases motivation at times of high appetitive behavior. - Galanin is a 29/30-amino acid long neuropeptide that has been implicated in many physiological and behavioral functions. Previous research has shown that i.c.v. administration of galanin strongly stimulates food intake in sated rats when food is freely available, but fails to stimulate this consumption when an operant response requirement is present. Using fixed ratio (FR) schedules, we sought to further clarify galanin's role in motivated behavior by administering galanin i.c.v. to rats working on fixed ratio schedules requiring either a low work condition (FR1) or higher work conditions (FR > 1) to obtain a 0.2% saccharin reward. Rats in the FR > 1 group were assigned to either an FR3, FR5 or FR7 schedule of reinforcement. The rate of reinforcement decreased for only the FR > 1 group as compared to saline controls. Furthermore, injections of GalR1 receptor agonist M617 led to a similar, marginally significant decrease in the number of reinforcers received in the FR > 1 condition, but a decrease was not seen after injections of GalR2 receptor agonist M1153. Taken together, these results show that galanin may be playing a role in decreasing motivation at times of high appetitive behavior, and that this effect is likely mediated by the GalR1 receptor. publications: Power Delivery Studies of Windbelt Generators with Different Architectures - Windbelt generators have been proposed as small, green power sources for battery charging applications. Some of the reported results lack detailed information about how key parameters influence the output power of the generator. In this work, we built prototypes with different architectures to study the voltage generation and power delivery as functions of belt tension, length, and electrical load at various wind speeds. We also studied the maximum power delivery conditions before the breakdown of the belt oscillation occurs. Our results are obtained from windbelt generators with two types of architectures: a conventional design with an adjustable belt that uses weight for tension control, and a revised design with a belt oscillation perpendicular to the coil axis. headline: Marketing Communications, Content Creator, Content Marketing, Writer, Managing Editor, Association Management, Event Marketing
summary: “With an edge but not over the edge.” That’s how I describe my marketing, writing, and content development style. I’m creative and resourceful, always looking for the angle to evolve the story in a unique way. My inquisitive nature drives my pursuit of the story, and my skills as an interviewer help me uncover the perspective that may be hiding below the surface. There have been many times someone told me that no one had ever asked them that question before. #gettingtowhy There is certainly a place for the fact-based, procedural message. But, as content marketers, the impact comes from the unexpected, the slight edge, that engages an audience. And then, what about bringing the story to life and reaching that audience? “I never give up and never fall apart until I get to plan ‘G’.” Plan ‘G’ would certainly be pushing my limits. Fortunately, I’ve never had to venture that far through the alphabet on a project. But I am a relentless project manager and contingency planner. I plan ahead for the project and plan in advance for possible next steps if the original plan gets derailed. I like to envision options. A project is like going to the ice cream shop: butter pecan in mind but having the chocolate cherry and coffee toffee on my radar if my first choice is not available. Of course, sometimes the best planning cannot cover every eventuality. An open mind led me to try a Blackberry Cabernet Sorbet, the most wonderful treat I had never heard of or ever imagined. I prefer waffle cones. A bowl and spoon is a great Plan ‘B.’
